newsitem.title: USA: Converse says wins suit against Apex sellers.
newsitem.headline: Converse says wins suit against Apex sellers.

text.p: Converse Inc. said Tuesday a jury awarded the athletic footwear maker $25.6 million in a lawsuit it filed against four former owners of Apex One Inc.
Apex One was acquired by Converse in June 1995 but sought Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in September.

Converse, the nation's largest manufacturer of athletic footwear, alleged breach of warranty and other claims against the defendants in a suit filed in the Supreme Court of the State of New York, in May 1996.
Apex One also had sued Converse for alleged violation of securities laws.
Converse said that due to contractual provisions in the Apex purchase and certain other agreements, the award would amount to about $13.7 million.
Converse said it expects to be paid an additional $2 million as a result of an agreement with another Apex seller.
The company, based in North Reading, Mass., said it did not know whether any of the defendants would pursue any post-trial motions or appeals.
Converse's stock edged up 12.5 cents to $14.375 on the New York Stock Exchange.
